log.text: Research done. Repo already runs whisper-server.exe (large-v3-turbo) with --vad --vad-model ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin (Servex/Servex.js:498-505) — the single biggest fix is already on. Report below.

REPORT (<400w): Options, cheapest/already-effort first.

1. VAD gating (Silero) — ALREADY ON in this repo. Servex.js:498-505 runs whisper-server.exe with `--vad --vad-model ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin`, model ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin. This is cited as 'the biggest win' for killing silence hallucinations (whisper.cpp issue #1026, github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/issues/1026). Risk: VAD can clip the start of real quiet speech if padding is too short; no padding flag is set here.

2. no_speech_thold / logprob_thold — whisper.cpp flags `-nth`/`-nst`-style thresholds exist but a 2026 report says whisper.cpp v1.9.2 returns 0.000 for every segment's no_speech_prob, making the threshold inert (github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/issues/960). Effort: add `--no-speech-thold`/`-mc 0` to the Servex.js args array, 1 line. Risk: may silently do nothing on this whisper.cpp build — verify with a log before trusting it.

3. `-mc 0` (max-context 0, i.e. condition_on_previous_text off) — stops one hallucinated window seeding a repeat loop in the next (same whisper.cpp issue #1026). Effort: 1 flag in Servex.js args. Risk: none significant; loses cross-segment context continuity for long dictation.

4. `--suppress-nst` / `-sns` (suppress non-speech tokens) — built into whisper.cpp. Effort: 1 flag. Risk: could drop legitimate filler tokens in rare cases.

5. Client-side energy/level gate before sending audio to Whisper — the Dictate mic stream already has raw audio; a simple RMS/dB floor skips calling whisper-server at all on near-silent chunks. Effort: a few lines in ux/Dictate's capture code (not located this pass). Risk: clipping real quiet speech if the floor is set too high; needs per-device tuning.

6. Hallucination phrase blocklist (post-filter: drop a transcript that is exactly 'Thank you.', 'Thanks for watching', 'you', etc. AND the segment's no_speech_prob is high or audio energy was near zero) — cheap backstop layered on top of VAD. Effort: a small list + check in WhisperLogRows.js or wherever transcripts land. Risk: could suppress a real utterance that happens to BE 'thank you' spoken quietly — gate it on low energy/no_speech, not on text alone. (dograh.com/feeds/blog/whisper-hallucination-silence, yaps.ai/blog/whisper-hallucination)

7. Model swap (large-v3 vs large-v3-turbo) — turbo (4 decoder layers vs 32, 809M vs 1.54B params) is ~4x faster with ~1-2% WER increase on same-language transcription; degrades more on some languages (gigagpu.com, huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo). No turbo-specific hallucination-rate data found. Not worth switching off turbo for this alone.

Recommend trying first: #3 (`-mc 0`) and #4 (`--suppress-nst`) — both are one-line flag additions to Servex.js's existing whisper-server args, zero new risk, and target exactly the repeat-hallucination mechanism VAD doesn't fully stop. Verify #2's no_speech_thold actually reports nonzero before relying on it.
